With a material volume constraint of 0.3, the topology optimized design shown in Fig. 4.2.1 was obtained. The optimized design is shown from multiple angles in Fig. 4.2.1. The optimized design reveals that bulk of the material from the center of the seatback can be removed. Topology optimized design of fully polymer composite seatback with material volume constraint of 0.3 Next, the compliance-based topology optimization minimizing material volume is extended to polymer composite seatback reinforced with the metal bracket. The multi-material controller-based optimization is performed using Tosca in ABAQUS. The optimized multi-material design is shown in Fig. 4.2.2. The optimized design confirmed that the bulk of the material can be removed from the center of the seatback while retaining the material at the shoulder belt location. The seatback frame would be designed using the inputs from the topology optimization as detailed in Section 4.3. Figure 4.2.2. Topology optimized design of polymer composite seatback with metal insert and material volume constraint of 0.3. 15 | P age 4.3 Subcomponent Design and Manufacturing In this section, the design of subcomponent which correspond to the maximum stress region within the seatback frame is detailed. The load carrying capacity of the polymer composite subcomponent is enhanced through the metal insert. The overall subcomponent is designed to be manufactured via the novel additive manufacturing – compression overmolding process without the need of any additional bonding mechanisms. The FE-based simulations for the subcomponent design were carried out using SolidWorks Static module. The iterative design process for the subcomponent started with the reference design shown in Fig. 4.3.1 (c), obtained using inputs from the topology optimization. The reference subcomponent and its constituents are illustrated in Fig. 4.3.2. The seatback subcomponent is made up of 3D printed metal bracket with a mesh design and long fiber thermoplastic reinforced with the unidirectional fibers on either side as shown in Fig. 4.3.2. First, the metal bracket with the mesh design will be fabricated using binder jet AM process. Next, this metal insert will be placed in a mold for additive manufacturing and compression overmolding of long fiber thermoplastic. The overmolded part will then be removed from the mold and cooled at the room temperature before reinforcing with unitape on either side. Finally, the subcomponent fabricated through this AM-CM process will be attached to the entire seatback frame through nuts and bolts as discussed in Section 4.4. Figure 4.3.1.
